verdict.rationale: Groq documents native tool/function calling: JSON-schema tool definitions passed via the tools parameter, function calling in the OpenAI-compatible Responses API, and remote MCP tool use where Groq handles all orchestration, which implies server-side multi-step tool loops. Nothing in the evidence shows parallel tool calls, explicit multi-step client-side loops, or any hands-on proof that tool calling is reliable. General community complaints about reliability are not specific to tool calling, so they only lower confidence. missing for 10: documented parallel tool calling, explicit multi-step/agent-loop docs for client-defined tools, strict-schema guarantees applied to tool arguments, independent corroboration of tool-call reliability on open models

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can rely on faithful function/tool calling — including parallel and multi-step tool use — so agent loops run on open models without breaking

citations.quote: To use tools, the model must be provided with tool definitions. These tool definitions are in JSON schema format and are passed to the model via the tools parameter
stateful conversations, and function calling to connect with external systems
Groq's Responses API supports remote tool use via MCP servers via HTTPS where Groq handles all orchestration
